body:
# D200 — Start #486 hosted verification during the Claude quota wait

The frozen #486 source is committed at 633d9ac72c10fe4b8d76f7ba50221f9ed8557cb9, tree d0e38c6c0212e312e6b605ac3d6bc8f7af5a129f. Its actual Fable review and Opus independent QA stopped on the provider quota and remain unfinished under D199. The complete local Windows coverage attempts failed; D195/D196 retain the failures and matching clean-baseline observations, and require the ordinary hosted coverage gate. Waiting to create a draft PR until Claude finishes would delay that independent platform verification without adding a technical gate.

Select a separate integration worktree and delivery branch from the frozen source, integrate current main through an ordinary merge with explicit parent/source/archive proof, then publish a draft PR to run normal CI. Keep both original author and independent QA checkouts at633 unchanged for the already-started provider work. No author, review or QA result is promoted to the integrated head without a documented source-equivalence/parent-combination proof. If integration changes #486 behavior, stop and reconcile that change with review and QA rather than treating it as equivalent.

The draft must disclose unfinished review/QA, both failed local coverage attempts, the matched-baseline limits, current CI and the later evidence archive/final audit still required. A preliminary CI pass only clears checks at its exact head/target; any later source, archive or target change needs the ordinary current-head/current-target gate again. No CI failure retry, threshold change, model substitution, extra formal review slot, paid overage, owner acceptance or merge is authorized by this scheduling decision.

Decline waiting idle for provider quota before discovering Linux-specific gate failures; decline weakening Windows tests or treating scoped successes as full coverage; decline changing the frozen review/QA worktrees in place; and decline treating a draft or preliminary green CI as completed delivery. This is an operational sequencing choice within admitted intent4 under delegated blocker authority, not admission of intent5 or an exception to a technical gate. The owner may review or rework it in the consolidated decision catalogue before owner QA.
